guarantees.claim: tick_baud_x16 is directly driven as the 16th bit of nco_sum_q.
tx_fifo_rready is the logical AND of tx_uart_idle, tx_fifo_rvalid, and tx_enable.

assumptions.claim: nco_sum_q[16] provides a clean, glitch-free baud tick aligned with the desired baud rate.
assumptions.cond: when baud timing is in use
assumptions.risk: Incorrect or glitchy nco_sum_q[16] yields erroneous baud timing, corrupting UART communication.

assumptions.claim: tx_uart_idle correctly indicates that the TX shift register is idle, tx_fifo_rvalid indicates valid data in the TX FIFO, and tx_enable is asserted only when transmission is permitted.
assumptions.risk: Premature assertion of tx_fifo_rready could read invalid data or violate handshake, leading to TX corruption or protocol violations.

uncertain_points.claim: The bit-index [16] on nco_sum_q assumes nco_sum_q has at least 17 bits. If the actual width is smaller, tick_baud_x16 will be out-of-bounds or constant.
uncertain_points.cond: if the module is parameterized with an insufficient NCO sum width.
uncertain_points.risk: Baud tick may become stuck or out-of-range, breaking UART timing.

uncertain_points.claim: tx_fifo_rready is purely combinational and may glitch if tx_fifo_rvalid changes combinatorially in response to a read, potentially creating a timing hazard in the handshake.
uncertain_points.cond: when tx_fifo_rvalid is updated in the same cycle as tx_fifo_rready assertion due to FIFO read
uncertain_points.risk: Could cause the TX logic to sample invalid data or violate handshake protocol, leading to transmit errors.
